## Front Matter (Secs. 1–7)

- **Sec. 1 Short title**: "Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024." Public Law 118-47; H.R. 2882; enacted Mar. 23, 2024. FY ending Sept. 30, 2024.
- **Sec. 2 Table of contents**: Divisions A–G (Defense; Financial Services/General Gov; Homeland Security; Labor-HHS-Education; Legislative Branch; State/Foreign Ops; Other Matters incl. Udall Foundation Reauthorization, UNRWA funding limitation, Budgetary Effects).

- **Sec. 4 Explanatory statement**: Statement in House Congressional Record ~Mar. 22, 2024, by House Appropriations chair, has same effect for divisions A–F as a joint conference committee statement.

## DIVISION A — DoD Appropriations Act, 2024 (general provisions)

**§8058** — Bars funds for repairs/maintenance to military family housing units, including areas used for official DoD business.

**§8059** — RDT&E Defense-Wide new-start defense innovation acceleration/rapid prototyping demo projects >$5M: obligation only 15 days after written report (project description, acquisition/transition strategy, annual+total cost) to congressional defense committees. SecDef may waive case-by-case by certifying national interest.

**§8060** — SecDef continues classified quarterly report to Approps Defense Subcommittees per classified annex.

**§8061** — Notwithstanding 10 USC 12310(b), National Guard member on full-time duty under 32 USC 502(f) may support ground-based elements of National Ballistic Missile Defense System.

**§8062** — No transfer to nongovernmental entities of DoD center-fire armor-piercing ammo ("armor penetrator/AP/API/API-T"), except demilitarization contractors that render projectiles unusable or manufacture ammo under DoD contract / for export under State Dept license.

**§8063** — Chief of NGB (or designee) may waive lease consideration under 10 USC 2667 for personal-property leases ≤1 year to organizations under 32 USC 508(d) or approved youth/social/fraternal nonprofits.

**§8064** — "Operation and Maintenance, Army": $175,943,968 available until expended; SecDef may transfer to other Federal Government activities; may contract for real property acquisition, construction, personal services, operations; may provide indemnification; projects must comply with Federal/State/local law to max extent consistent with national security.

**§8065** — Bars modifying: (1) National Intelligence Program (NIP) appropriations account structure; (2) budget presentation in P-1/R-1/O-1; (3) apportionment process; (4) allotment/obligation/disbursement process. Permits mergers/changes at/below Expenditure Center level. DNI + SecDef may jointly study alternative financial management processes for auditability (incl. counterintelligence risk assessment); must provide proposals to affected agencies, get certifications, present to defense+intel committees within 30 days of receiving certifications.

**§8066** — Appropriates $100,000,000 for transfer to O&M/procurement/RDT&E for AFRICOM/SOUTHCOM cooperation with allies/partners. No obligation until 30 days after execution plan to defense committees; notify ≥15 days before transfer.

**§8067** — Up to $11,000,000 from each of O&M Army, Navy, Air Force transferable to Fisher Houses/Suites central fund per 10 USC 2493(d).

**§8068** — Appropriates $5,000,000, available until expended; upon SecDef national-interest determination, only for grant to Fisher House Foundation, Inc. for constructing/furnishing additional Fisher Houses.

**§8069** — Up to $1,000,000 of O&M Navy for transfer to John C. Stennis Center Trust Fund (2 USC 1105).

**§8070** — Bars modifying command/control to give Fleet Forces Command control of Pacific fleet forces; Oct 1, 2004 relationships remain until written modification proposed; implementable 30 days after notice unless House/Senate Approps objects; cannot preclude INDOPACOM commander's operational requirements.

## §7046 (cont.) — Assistance to Former Soviet States / Turkey / Ukraine
- Exceptions to WMD/nonprolif restrictions listed: (1) WMD Act 1996 §1424 (50 USC 2333) or nonproliferation aid; (2) Trade & Dev. Agency aid (FAA §661); (3) US & Foreign Commercial Service official acts; (4) DFC insurance/guarantees (BUILD Act 2018, div F PL 115-254); (5) Ex-Im Bank financing (PL 79-173); (6) humanitarian assistance.
- **(b) Territorial integrity**: no funds for a former-Soviet gov't violating another's sovereignty (Helsinki Final Act); Presidential waiver on national security determination; prior consultation with Approps required.
- **(c) Turkey**: no funds to sell defense articles/services to Turkish Presidential Protection Directorate (TPPD) under AECA ch.2 unless Sec. State certifies TPPD members named in July 17, 2017 DC Superior Court indictment returned/brought to justice. Exceptions: border security, NATO/coalition ops, protection of US officials/facilities in Turkey.
- **(d) Ukraine**:
  - Strategy due within **60 days** to leadership/committees; goals, benchmarks, timelines, staffing.
  - **Cost matching**: ESF + AEECA contributions to Gov't of Ukraine may not exceed **50%** of total from all sources; Presidential waiver on national security determination; report every **120 days**; requirement continues until funds expended.
  - Oversight: staffing (titles I/II); in-person monitoring; joint State/USAID certification **15 days** before initial obligation (ESF, AEECA, INCLE, NADR, FMF); §7015(e) applies; §1706 of Additional Ukraine Supp. Approps Act 2023 (div M PL 117-328) applies to titles I–IV Ukraine funds.
  - Reports: comprehensive report **60 days** then every **90 days** (assistance since Feb 24, 2022); use-of-funds report **90 days** then every **90 days**. Public per §7016(b).

## §7047 — Countering Russian Influence & Aggression
- **(a)** No funds for central Gov't of Russian Federation.
- **(b) Annexation**: no funds for central gov't supporting Russian annexation of Crimea/Ukraine territory; Sec. State waiver (national interest); bars recognition of Russian sovereignty, US investment facilitation, assistance involving Russian officials/entities; Treasury to direct US IFI directors to oppose assistance violating Ukraine sovereignty; ends when Ukraine reestablishes sovereignty.
- **(c) Georgia (Abkhazia/South Ossetia)**: no funds for central gov't recognizing independence/establishing diplomatic relations; State to publish list; Sec. State waiver; no funds to support occupation; Treasury IFI opposition.
- **(d) Countering Russian Influence Fund**: **≥$300,000,000** (from AEECA, INCLE, IMET, FMF) per §254 of Countering Russian Influence Act 2017 (PL 115-44; 22 USC 9543), notwithstanding subsection (b) country limit. FMF funds available until **Sept 30, 2025**.
